latencyReports.latencyScope: individual synchronous calls, from before request ID assignment and input decoding through final groups/IDs/flags; includes pool admission and transport; excludes workload dispatch, preflight, pool startup and shutdown; throughput is closed-loop wall throughput at the stated caller concurrency
latencyReports.resourceScope: fresh test subprocess per lane/workload/concurrency; steady-state host RSS plus only that lane's live workers; baseline before pool creation; warmup/steady initial after first request, preflight, GC and measurement-buffer allocation
latencyReports.resourceLimitations: 10ms sampled RSS can miss short peaks and sampler contention can affect latency; aggregate is summed at each observation, not a sum of independent peaks, and double-counts shared pages; host includes test runtime and workload fixtures; Rust workers have no Go goroutine count; threads and RSS may remain retained after close; startup/first-request distributions are serial fresh size-one pools and have no sampled resource peaks; row startup is through all pool workers READY; the single first request in each row is before preflight; steady samples exclude both and preflight warmup

limitations: Schema 3 retains row percentile summaries, not individual durations; percentiles cannot be reconstructed.
Short rows with only initial/final RSS cannot establish memory stability; 10ms sampling can miss peaks.
Go allocations exclude Rust allocator activity.
Unpinned shared loaded host and seeded row order can cause crossings; three-run medians are narrow screening evidence.
Startup groups are ordered, ten fresh size-one pools per workload, without cold-cache comparison.
No native arm64 execution, full matrix, production bridge selection or wiring.
